te: Progress on declaring Khelang Banphot National Park, Lampang
se: The committee followed up the declaration of Khelang Banphot National Park in Lampang, begun in 2016 and not yet complete, with the Office of the Permanent Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation and Protected Area Regional Office 13 (Lampang branch) invited. Reasons for the delay include the change of the national parks law (from 1961 to 2019), which required waiting for a regulation on public hearings, overlap with a land reform area, and a 2024 Cabinet resolution requiring boundary maps to be revised under the One Map project first.
it: Progress on declaring Khelang Banphot National Park, Lampang

te: Encroachment on forest and land reform land in Muak Lek, Saraburi
se: The committee studied the facts of encroachment on forest and land reform land in Muak Lek district, Saraburi, where it is claimed that land reform land was held and bought unlawfully to put up buildings. The Royal Forest Department, the Agricultural Land Reform Office and the National Office of Buddhism were invited. The Land Reform Office said it found the encroachment in 2024 and has acted under its procedures. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Encroachment on forest and land reform land, Muak Lek district, Saraburi

te: Following up measures to reduce conflict between people and wild elephants
se: The committee continued with the problems of wild elephants and villagers along forest edges, and land use in land reform areas overlapping forest, in Si Chomphu district, Khon Kaen, and Phu Kradueng district, Loei. The Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, the Royal Forest Department, the Agricultural Land Reform Office, the National Land Policy Office and animal foundations were invited, to find structural measures that reduce conflict and the loss of both human and elephant lives.
it: Measures to reduce conflict between people and wild elephants (Khon Kaen, Loei)

te: The Khlong Phrao reservoir on Ko Chang, partly inside a national park
se: The committee considered a complaint from the Senators Meet the People project in the East about the Khlong Phrao reservoir in Ko Chang district, Trat, which helps solve water shortages on Ko Chang, but part of which lies inside Mu Ko Chang National Park. Revoking that part of the park is not finished because of legal steps, such as the integrated state land boundary map (One Map) not yet being complete. The Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation was invited.
it: The Khlong Phrao reservoir partly inside Mu Ko Chang National Park, Trat

te: The Sing Buri Sandbox, and alternate wetting and drying rice farming to cut greenhouse gases
se: The committee studied the Sing Buri Sandbox project and support for low-carbon organic farming, such as alternate wetting and drying in rice fields, to cut greenhouse gases from rice farming. Sing Buri's plan has six parts: clean energy, environment-friendly transport, green space, a low-carbon economy, waste and wastewater management, and public participation.
it: The Sing Buri Sandbox and alternate wetting and drying rice farming

te: Wild elephants and villagers, and land reform land overlapping forest in Khon Kaen and Loei
se: The committee considered a complaint asking for follow-up on wild elephant problems, to reduce conflict between wild elephants and people who live and farm along forest edges, and for a check of resorts, holiday homes and cafés in land reform areas that overlap national reserved forest and national parks in Si Chomphu district, Khon Kaen, and Phu Kradueng district, Loei. The matter began with the death of a wild elephant during relocation. The meeting observed that non-farming businesses on land reform land may not match the purpose of land reform. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Wild elephants and villagers, and land reform land overlapping forest (Khon Kaen, Loei)

te: Complaint about land reform documents in Bang Lamung, Chon Buri
se: The committee considered a complaint from members of the public that land reform documents may have been issued wrongly in Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri, possibly not following the 1995 agreement between the Royal Forest Department and the Agricultural Land Reform Office on returning national reserved forest land. The claims include documents over headwater forest and a public stream, the eligibility of land holders, and about 173 rai of forest that a court has already ordered returned. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint about land reform documents over forest, Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri

te: Following up the 2,256-million-baht urgent project against forest encroachment
se: The committee continued to hear about the urgent project to stop encroachment on the country's forests, funded with 2,256 million baht from the Environment Fund, with the Office of the Permanent Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment, the Royal Forest Department, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources, the Department of Special Investigation (DSI) and the Office of the NACC invited. The Office of the Permanent Secretary explained the background, how the project was prepared and why it used the Environment Fund instead of the central budget.
it: Background and progress of the 2,256-million-baht urgent project against forest encroachment

te: Three subcommittees set up, and the urgent project against forest encroachment
se: The meeting resolved to set up three subcommittees: Land Resources (chaired by Mr. Jirasak Chukwamdee), Whole-System Water Management, Pollution and Environment (chaired by Miss Ratchaneekorn Thongthip) and Climate Change and Air Pollution (chaired by Mr. Chavaphon Wattanavekin). It then began considering the urgent project to stop encroachment on the country's forests, funded by the Environment Fund, with the agencies concerned invited.
it: Three subcommittees set up (land resources; water and pollution; climate and air pollution)
Urgent project against forest encroachment, funded by the Environment Fund

te: Low-carbon cities and the Mae La Sandbox project
se: The committee heard the Department of Climate Change and Environment on low-carbon cities and plans for the Mae La Sandbox, a model for moving to a low-carbon society and a hub for carbon credits from farming and wetlands, as well as Thailand's greenhouse gas target (NDC 3.0). It then took up a complaint asking for a check of a land use certificate on a hilltop at Ao Chak, Suk Samran district, Ranong, and set the next meeting date.
it: Low-carbon cities and the Mae La Sandbox (Department of Climate Change and Environment)
Complaint about a land document on a hilltop, Ao Chak, Ranong

te: Seized ore in Mae Hong Son, and lead ore piles at an old mine in Kanchanaburi
se: The committee considered two matters. The first was seized fluorite ore kept on people's farmland (land reform land) in Mueang Paeng, Pai district, Mae Hong Son. The second was land use around the Song Tho mine in Thong Pha Phum district, Kanchanaburi, closed for more than 20 years and still holding large piles of lead ore, which worry local people. The Department of Primary Industries and Mines, the Royal Forest Department and the two provincial industry offices were invited.
it: Seized fluorite ore on farmland, Pai district, Mae Hong Son
Lead ore piles at an old mine, Thong Pha Phum district, Kanchanaburi

te: Dredging the Tha Chin River so water drains better
se: The committee considered ways to improve drainage by dredging the Tha Chin River in Chai Nat, Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom and Samut Sakhon, with the Marine Department, the Royal Irrigation Department and the Office of the National Water Resources (ONWR) invited. The main problem is that the river keeps silting up and dredging is not yet planned along the whole river. The Marine Department dredges selected spots each year within its budget and has asked for a budget to study and design dredging of the whole system, while the Royal Irrigation Department is building shortcut canals so water flows straighter and drains faster.
it: Ways to dredge the Tha Chin River for better drainage (Marine Department, Royal Irrigation Department, ONWR)
